feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Devastating storms continue to hit Southwest 'Four Corners' region
entry.summary: Communities in the Southwest are bracing for more flooding this weekend. This follows weeks of devastating storms that have pummeled parts of the region.

entry.title: What a midterm race in Kentucky says about how Democrats may do in Trump strongholds
entry.summary: Democrats are putting up a fight in midterm races this year that went for President Donald Trump by double digits in 2024. Kentucky Public Radio's Sylvia Goodman explains what we can learn from one Kentucky district.

entry.title: Mixed economic forecast weighs heavy ahead of midterms
entry.summary: There was a mixed Halloween bag of economic news this week. GDP growth is up, but so are prices. For now at least, interest rates are staying the same. What does that mean for the midterm elections?

entry.title: Secretary Rubio has a tough time getting officials at G20 on the same page
entry.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is hosting the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, with a focus on economic and security challenges.

entry.title: Pianist and podcaster on the timeless joy of jazz music
entry.summary: NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer speaks with Jazz pianist Joe Alterman about his podcast The Upside of Jazz from NPR member stations WABE in Atlanta.

entry.title: A new political era in the Southern Philippines
entry.summary: A new local government has taken its seat in the southern Philippines, in a step that marks a milestone in the peace process for a conflict that has lasted some 80 years.

entry.title: Election officials worry about DOJ monitoring of Tuesday's vote
entry.summary: Some election officials have been notified that the DOJ will be monitoring their polling stations. NPR's voting correspondent Miles Parks explains what he's watching for on election day - and afterwards.

entry.title: The art and science of a scream
entry.summary: What does it take to create a horror movie scream that is truly horrifying? One that makes the hair on the back of your neck stand up? NPR's Michelle Aslam found it is part art and part science.

entry.title: 100 years later, Harry Houdini's death still haunts Detroit
entry.summary: The legacy of magician Harry Houdini still looms large in Detroit 100 years after his death there. Some mark the anniversary of Houdini's death by trying to make contact with his spirit.

entry.title: Halloween temperatures have been trending hotter. Here's what the data shows
entry.summary: Recent analysis from research nonprofit Climate Central found that on average, fall temperatures have warmed by 2.9 degrees Fahrenheit in the U.S. and the summer heat is lasting longer.
